population_trend_notes: Alentejo region population trajectory 2011-2021 was -6.9% per INE Censos 2021, with persistent rural depopulation partially offset by inbound EU retirees and lifestyle migrants since 2018.
median_age_notes: Median age ~50 years in 2023, oldest of Portugal's NUTS-II regions per Pordata.
migration_notes: Net rural decline offset by inbound migration of EU retirees, French/German/Dutch/Belgian lifestyle migrants and digital nomads, especially in Alto and Baixo Alentejo coastal strip.
rural_density_notes: Alentejo population density ~22 inhabitants/km2 in 2023, roughly one-eighth Portugal's national average of ~111/km2.
source: accessibility.md, INE Portugal Censos 2021 and Pordata 2023

population_trend_notes: Interior Ourense province has lost ~15% of population since 2000 per IGE; net negative for interior with coastal areas stable.
median_age_notes: Median age ~49.5 years in 2023, Spain's oldest NUTS-II region by median age per INE 2023.
migration_notes: Net negative for interior; positive net migration into coastal towns; neorrural return-to-village movement statistically marginal but locally visible.
rural_density_notes: Galicia overall density ~91 inhabitants/km2 in 2023, close to Spain national 95/km2, but bimodal with coastal arc dense and interior Ourense/Lugo at depopulation-frontier densities.
source: accessibility.md, IGE Galicia and INE 2023

population_trend_notes: Romania national rural population trajectory 2011-2021 was -9.6% per INS Census 2021; many rural villages have lost 30-50% of population since 1990 while Cluj-Napoca grows.
median_age_notes: Median age in rural Transylvania 2022: ~46 years; in Cluj-Napoca 2022: ~38 years.
migration_notes: Dominant emigration outflow (~3-4 million Romanians abroad); modest return migration post-2020; Saxon-village foreign-resident pockets in Sibiu and Brasov counties grew through 2023-2024.
rural_density_notes: Centru and Nord-Vest NUTS-II regions density ~70 inhabitants/km2 per 2022 Census, with Cluj concentration and thin rural backcountry.
source: accessibility.md, INS Recensamantul Populatiei 2021

population_trend_notes: The trend differs by area, so no single direction fits: West Cork saw significant in-migration through 2020 to 2024, while the Connemara Gaeltacht core is declining slowly with Údarás na Gaeltachta investment.
median_age_notes: Median age in rural West Cork 2022: ~42 years; Connemara Gaeltacht core: ~43 years per CSO Census 2022.
migration_notes: West Cork net positive driven by remote-work and lifestyle migration; Connemara Gaeltacht core net negative slowly.
rural_density_notes: West Cork ~29 inhabitants/km2 and Connemara/Galway West ~22 inhabitants/km2 per CSO Census 2022, vs Ireland national ~73/km2.
source: accessibility.md, CSO Ireland Census 2022

population_trend_notes: Pembrokeshire population stable-to-slightly-declining since 2011; coastal areas see seasonal and retirement in-migration; rural inland wards lose young adults.
median_age_notes: Median age in Pembrokeshire 2021 Census: ~46 years vs Wales 42, UK 40.
migration_notes: Coastal towns receive in-migration from across the UK and (post-Brexit) reduced inflow from continental Europe; rural inland wards lose young adults.
rural_density_notes: Pembrokeshire ~78 inhabitants/km2 per 2021 Census; rural ward density materially lower at 10-30/km2.
source: accessibility.md, ONS Census 2021

population_trend_notes: Net positive migration into Lozere and rural Gard 2015-2024 driven by remote workers, retirees, and neo-ruraux; population growth in Lozere reversed long-term decline modestly.
median_age_notes: Median age in Lozere 2024: ~46 years per INSEE 2024.
migration_notes: Cevennes-area communes show positive net migration since 2015 per INSEE migration data 2020-2024; neo-rural wave continues.
rural_density_notes: Lozere ~15 inhabitants/km2 in 2024, France's lowest departement density; National Park des Cevennes ~24/km2 across 2,930 km2.
source: accessibility.md, INSEE 2024

population_trend_notes: Population growth 2011 to 2023: +5.3% per ASTAT, positive trajectory unusual for European mountain regions.
median_age_notes: Median age 2024: ~43 years, younger than Italy national ~47 and rural-Italy norm per ASTAT 2024.
migration_notes: Positive net migration including from Italy, Germany, Austria, and increasingly from Eastern Europe.
rural_density_notes: South Tirol ~72 inhabitants/km2 in 2024 (~535,000 across ~7,400 km2) per ASTAT.
source: accessibility.md, ASTAT 2024

population_trend_notes: Population 2011 to 2023: -6.4% per INE/SADEI; steep depopulation in interior valleys and Cantabrian mountains; birth rate among Europe's lowest.
median_age_notes: Median age Asturias 2024: ~50.4 years, the oldest of Spain's 17 autonomous communities per INE 2024.
migration_notes: Net negative overall; modest inflow of urban-fleeing repobladores, retirees, and Latin American (especially Venezuelan and Colombian) migrants since 2018, not enough to reverse decline.
rural_density_notes: Asturias regional density ~95 inhabitants/km2 in 2023 but heavily concentrated in Oviedo-Gijon-Aviles belt; rural-interior comarca densities 10-30/km2.
source: accessibility.md, SADEI and INE 2023-2024

population_trend_notes: Lost population continuously since 1990; population 2011 to 2023: -4.5% per LSA 2024, with continued decline projected.
median_age_notes: Median age 2024: ~48 years, among Germany's oldest per Destatis 2024.
migration_notes: Continuous net out-migration since 1990; modest stabilisation post-2015 in metropolitan Halle/Magdeburg; rural depopulation continues; foreign-resident share remains low (~7%) but growing.
rural_density_notes: State ~106 inhabitants/km2 in 2024; rural Landkreis density e.g. Altmarkkreis Salzwedel: ~32/km2 per LSA 2024.
source: accessibility.md, Statistisches Landesamt Sachsen-Anhalt 2024

population_trend_notes: Estonia's overall population stabilised post-2017 after long decline (return migration of diaspora plus Ukrainian refugees post-2022); rural Setomaa continues to decline; Saaremaa stable or modestly positive.
median_age_notes: Median age Estonia 2024: ~42 years per Statistikaamet 2024.
migration_notes: Return migration of diaspora plus Ukrainian refugees post-2022 stabilised national population; Saaremaa sees modest in-migration of remote workers; Setomaa declines.
rural_density_notes: Estonia national density ~30 inhabitants/km2 in 2024; Saaremaa ~12/km2 (~30,000 people on ~2,673 km2); Setomaa parish density ~5-7/km2.
source: accessibility.md, Statistics Estonia / Statistikaamet 2024

population_trend_notes: Three wards (footprint plus Small Isles): 25,992 (mid-2011), 25,803 (2016), 26,319 (mid-2021) per National Records of Scotland estimates on 2022 wards; Census 2022 26,859 (citypopulation.de, attributed NRS). Census 2011 to 2022 by ward: North, West and Central Sutherland 6,130 to 5,791; Wester Ross, Strathpeffer and Lochalsh 12,230 to 12,196; Caol and Mallaig 8,790 to 8,872.
median_age_notes: Median age (computed from NRS single-year ages, three wards): 47 (mid-2011), 50 (2016), 51 (mid-2021) against Scotland 41, 41, 42; share aged 65 and over 21.5, 24.7, 26.2 percent (Scotland 16.9, 18.5, 19.6); under-16s 16.9 to 13.8 percent (Scotland 17.3 to 16.6).
migration_notes: A flat population with a median age rising about four years in a decade implies in-migration offsetting natural decrease, but ward-level migration components were not opened; not asserted.
rural_density_notes: GHSL 2030 over the footprint 2.3 p/km2; Census 2022 over the three wards 2.3 p/km2 (ward range 1.2 to 4.3; Caol is a Fort William suburb and Strathpeffer is Inverness commuter belt) against Scotland about 70.
source: National Records of Scotland, Electoral ward population estimates (mid-2001 to mid-2021, 2022 wards); Scotland's Census 2022 via citypopulation.de
gaps: Highlands and Islands Enterprise population work and Census 2022 ward age tables were not opened; migration components not found.

population_trend_notes: 18 footprint municipalities: 253,464 (1990) to 219,348 (2025), -13.5%; the 14 smaller municipalities 124,574 to 76,809, -38.3%; Joensuu, Kontiolahti and Liperi grew; 15 of 18 shrank. Statistics Finland projection 2024: 220,356 (2024), 215,592 (2030), 208,607 (2040), 206,034 (2045), -5.3% 2024 to 2040.
median_age_notes: Mean age 46.9 (national 44.1) and 29.6% aged 65+ (national 23.8%), 31 Dec 2025, population-weighted over the 18 municipalities; outside Joensuu and Kajaani mean age 50.5 and 35.4% 65+. The statistic is the mean, not the median.
migration_notes: Intermunicipal net migration across the 18 municipalities: -538 (2020), -298, -1,055, -1,261, -1,406, -1,468 (2025). International migration not included; foreign citizens are 5.4% of residents (3.4% outside the two hubs).
rural_density_notes: 7.4 persons per km2 land area (national 18.6); 4.1 outside Joensuu and Kajaani; municipal densities from 1.4 (Ristijärvi) to 33.2 (Joensuu).
source: Statistics Finland, tables 11ra, 14wx, 11a2 (opened via PxWeb API 2026-10-04)
gaps: Municipal projection uses the 2024 projection round and the 2024 municipal division (Nurmes already includes the former Valtimo).

population_trend_notes: Sum of the 124 communes (INSEE, municipal population): 55,189 (1968), 40,515 (1999), 39,298 (2011), 38,950 (2016), 38,564 (2020), 38,746 (2023). Fifty years of loss have slowed to a plateau; 2011 to 2023 is -1.4%, 2020 to 2023 +0.5%.
median_age_notes: INSEE RP 2021 age bands: 32.7% aged 65 or over (France, all communes 20.5%), 10.7% aged 80 or over (6.1%); median roughly 54, interpolated from bands (France about 42).
migration_notes: The Parc's own count: migration balance +427 against natural change -469 (annual variation -42; period label ambiguous on its page, INSEE RP 2016-2022). Arrivals offset, but do not exceed, natural decline.
rural_density_notes: 11.6 inhabitants per km2 (38,746 / 3,352); median commune 7.6; seven communes above 1,000 inhabitants (Meymac, Eymoutiers, Felletin, Chamberet, Treignac, Corrèze, Peyrat-le-Château) hold 28% of residents.
source: INSEE, Historique des populations communales 1876-2023; INSEE RP 2021 TD_POP1A; Parc naturel régional de Millevaches (revitalisation study page)
gaps: Period of the Parc migration figures is ambiguously labelled on its page; median age is interpolated from bands, not published.

population_trend_notes: Footprint 86,954 (2011) to 83,172 (1 Jan 2025): -4.3%; outside Teruel city 51,666 to 46,517: -10.0%. Since the 2021 Padron the total is +2.0% (81,539 to 83,172); 90 of 180 municipalities grew 2021-25 (85 declined, 5 unchanged), and 37 grew over 2011-25 (140 declined, 3 unchanged). Maestrazgo -15.9% since 2011 and -3.9% since 2021; Cuencas Mineras -13.8%. INE Padron cifras oficiales, table 2899.
median_age_notes: Mean age 46.7 and 24.6% aged 65 or more (population-weighted over the six comarcas, IAEST fichas, INE annual census 1 Jan 2025): Maestrazgo 50.3 / 30.4%, Sierra de Albarracin 50.6 / 28.6%, Gudar-Javalambre 45.6 / 22.5%. Median age itself not published at this level.
migration_notes: Foreign-national share 13.1% (weighted; Jiloca 17.6%, Gudar-Javalambre 16.3%, Albarracin 9.3%, IAEST 2025); the post-2021 gain is small and uneven; 85 of 180 municipalities are under 100 inhabitants.
rural_density_notes: 7.5 p/km2 over 11,090 km2 (INE 2025), 4.4 outside Teruel city; median municipality 110 inhabitants; 158 of 180 under 500.
source: INE Padron (table 2899), IAEST Estadistica Local fichas for the six comarcas
gaps: Median age not published; INE 2021 base partly reflects the 2021 census revision.

population_trend_notes: ISTAT 1 January: 13 comuni 11,555 (2019) to 11,458 (2025), -0.8 percent; the 11 mountain comuni 2,953 to 2,892, -2.1 percent. Long run is a century of loss in the high communes (Pettenati 2013: Macra 861 in 1931 to 52 in 2011; ISTAT 2025: 42).
median_age_notes: ISTAT 2025: median age 49 over the 13 comuni and 53 in the 11 mountain comuni; 65 and over are 25.7 and 29.2 percent, under-15s 12.5 and 9.8 percent. National comparison not opened.
migration_notes: ISTAT registry flows 2019 to 2024: 13 comuni net +528 (internal -9, foreign +537; Dronero alone +345); 11 mountain comuni net +104 (internal +56, foreign +48) against natural change of -154 (101 births, 255 deaths). Arrivals offset about two thirds of natural loss in the mountain comuni; foreign flows are not newcomer-settler counts.
rural_density_notes: 20.1 per km2 over the 13 comuni (ISTAT 2025 over OSM boundary area 568.8 km2), 5.9 per km2 over the 11 mountain comuni; Dronero holds 61 percent of residents.
source: ISTAT POSAS 2019-2025 and Bilancio demografico mensile 2019-2024; Pettenati 2013
gaps: Registry flows are all moves, not purpose-built newcomer counts; Pettenati's evidence is newcomer-side only; ISTAT national median age not opened.

population_trend_notes: Oregon's population grew 10.6% 2010-2020 per US Census 2020, driven primarily by net in-migration from California; Lane, Benton, and Linn counties all recorded positive net migration 2015-2022.
median_age_notes: Median age in Oregon 2022: 39.7 years per US Census ACS 2022, younger than EU peer regions with a significantly younger in-migration stream.
migration_notes: Net-attracting younger, educated migrants from California and across the US, including people moving for climate reasons (dossier statement, not verified); an arriving community, not an ageing, shrinking one.
rural_density_notes: Willamette Valley regional average ~55 persons/km2 per JRC GHSL R2023; rural hinterland 5-30/km2 with urban cores (Salem ~2,000/km2, Eugene ~1,800/km2).
source: accessibility.md, JRC GHSL R2023 and US Census 2020

population_trend_notes: Vermont is the second least-populated state in the US after Wyoming; population is ageing and the rural workforce is thin; back-to-the-land migration history (35,000+ new rural settlers 1968-1975) seeded persistent regen culture.
migration_notes: Back-to-the-land migration (the 1970s counterculture wave seeded durable infrastructure) and a newer wave of migrants who say they move for climate reasons; both are dossier statements and were not verified.
rural_density_notes: Vermont statewide population density 27 persons/km2 per US Census 2020 (49th lowest state); highly rural counties Essex 9/km2 and Orleans 15/km2; agricultural/forested interior of central Vermont ~5-15 persons/km2.
source: accessibility.md, US Census Bureau 2020 Decennial Census
gaps: Dossier does not give an explicit Vermont median age number, only references ageing population qualitatively.

population_trend_notes: In-migration into Western North Carolina of back-to-the-land and climate-motivated movers (dossier statement, not verified); Asheville Communities Network catalogued 41 intentional communities in beginning stages in WNC alone as of 2025.
migration_notes: Regen-driven in-migration, including people moving for climate reasons, has pushed land prices up (dossier statement, not verified); the region has 30 years of institutional depth attracting practitioners.
rural_density_notes: Western NC 18-county regional density ~47 persons/km2 per WNC Vitality Index 2022; Buncombe County (Asheville hub) ~120-158/km2; surrounding rural counties (Haywood, Madison, Yancey, Mitchell, Avery) 15-40/km2.
source: accessibility.md, WNC Vitality Index and US Census 2020
gaps: Dossier does not give explicit median age data for WNC.

population_trend_notes: Dossier describes density and infrastructure but does not give an explicit recent population trend direction for the core Driftless counties.
rural_density_notes: Driftless core counties per 2020 Census: Vernon ~15.0 persons/km2, Crawford ~10.9/km2, Richland ~11.3/km2; 5-county regional average ~18.9/km2.
source: accessibility.md, US Census Bureau 2020 Decennial Census
gaps: Dossier omits explicit recent population trend, median age, and migration figures for the Driftless core.

population_trend_notes: Most Ozark counties have lost population in every census since 1980; Newton County had 7,225 people in 2020 (US Census); the historical peak of about 13,000 and the Searcy County figure were not verified.
median_age_notes: Older median age 45-50 in core counties per accessibility.md demographic profile.
migration_notes: Outmigration of working-age adults dominant since 1980; Starlink-enabled first wave of knowledge-economy workers relocating to the region is a positive demographic signal but not enough to reverse decline.
rural_density_notes: Newton County, AR: 3.4 persons/km2; Searcy County: 4.5/km2; Stone County: 7.9/km2 per US Census 2020 (Stone County: 12,359 people over 20.375 square miles); the JRC GHSL rural classification was not re-checked.
source: accessibility.md, US Census Bureau 2020

population_trend_notes: Dossier does not give explicit recent population trend direction for Taos County.
migration_notes: Dossier notes earthship and arts/tourism economy attract practitioners and inflate land values via earthship B and B and short-term rental operators, but does not quantify recent net migration.
rural_density_notes: Taos County population density 6.05 persons/km2 per US Census 2020 (population 34,489; land area 5,710 km2); 54.6% of residents live in rural areas.
source: accessibility.md, US Census Bureau 2020
gaps: Dossier omits explicit recent population trend, median age, and net migration data for Taos County.

population_trend_notes: Dossier provides density and economic context but does not give an explicit recent population trend direction for Nova Scotia or Cape Breton.
migration_notes: Immigration-friendly context noted (international collaborators can join within 1-2 year pathway); NS PNP quota cut 50% in 2025 is referenced in MEMORY but not visible in these dossier files.
rural_density_notes: Nova Scotia provincial density 18.4 persons/km2 per Statistics Canada 2021 Census; Cape Breton Island overall ~38.7/km2 but Inverness County only ~6.1/km2; rural Cape Breton Highlands 2-5/km2.
source: accessibility.md, Statistics Canada 2021 Census
gaps: Dossier omits explicit recent population trend, median age, and migration figures for Nova Scotia.

population_trend_notes: Dossier covers density and intentional-community depth but does not give an explicit recent population trend direction for the Central Kootenay.
rural_density_notes: Regional District of Central Kootenay density 2.8 persons/km2 per Statistics Canada 2021 Census (62,509 people over 22,265 km2); electoral sub-districts range from 0.3/km2 to 23.8/km2; Nelson city ~820/km2.
source: accessibility.md, Statistics Canada 2021 Census
gaps: Dossier omits explicit recent population trend, median age, and migration figures for the Kootenays.

population_trend_notes: Dossier covers density and accessibility but does not give an explicit recent population trend direction for Estrie.
migration_notes: Proximity to Montreal creates second-home demand pushing rural land prices upward through 2000s-2020s; no explicit migration data given.
rural_density_notes: Estrie administrative region ~33 persons/km2 per Statistics Canada 2021 Census (337,701 residents over 10,212 km2); Sherbrooke core >1,000/km2 with agricultural rural areas 5-20/km2.
source: accessibility.md, Statistics Canada 2021 Census
gaps: Dossier omits explicit recent population trend, median age, and migration figures for Estrie.

population_trend_notes: Dossier provides 2020 census totals and municipal fragmentation context but does not give an explicit recent population trend direction for the highlands.
rural_density_notes: Oaxaca state overall ~44 hab/km2 per INEGI Census 2020 (4,132,148 people over 93,758 km2); Valles Centrales jurisdiction 80.8/km2; Sierra Norte jurisdiction 22.9/km2.
source: accessibility.md, INEGI Censo de Poblacion y Vivienda 2020
gaps: Dossier omits explicit recent population trend, median age, and net migration data for Oaxaca highlands.

population_trend_notes: Five-county total 260,532 (2010 Census) to 258,474 (2020) = -0.8 percent; NYS estimates 258,470 (2020 base) to 253,282 (2024) = -2.0 percent with all five counties lower in 2024 than 2020. Tompkins +4.1 percent 2010-20 and -1.3 percent 2020-24; the other four -2.3 to -4.7 percent 2010-20.
median_age_notes: Not retrievable: api.census.gov required a key; data.census.gov and QuickFacts returned 403.
migration_notes: No migration series opened. Amish and Mennonite in-migration (an expectation from pre-research) not verified at county level: NY Amish population 25,220 in 60 settlements statewide (Young Center, 2025); Census of Agriculture shows Yates farms -3 percent 2017-22.
rural_density_notes: Census 2020: 46.3 persons/km2 over the five counties' land area (258,474 / 5,585 km2); Tompkins 86.0, Cayuga 42.6, Seneca 40.3, Yates 28.3, Schuyler 21.0; 35.1 outside Tompkins. GHSL R2023A 2030 over the footprint including lakes: 36.1.
source: US Census Bureau TIGERweb Census 2010 and 2020; NYS Open Data population estimates (krt9-ym2k); JRC GHSL R2023A
gaps: Median age, migration flows, Amish/Mennonite settlement by county.

population_trend_notes: Census 2020 101,099 (Louisa 37,596, Orange 36,254, Fluvanna 27,249). 2025 estimates (Census, via Wikipedia): Louisa 42,924 (+14.2%), Orange 40,083 (+10.6%), Fluvanna 28,975 (+6.3%); total 111,982 (+10.8%). Weldon Cooper Center July 2025 projection: 114,363 in 2030, 122,352 in 2040, 136,307 in 2050.
median_age_notes: Median age 2020: Louisa 45.2, Orange 44.6, Fluvanna 44.5 (Wikipedia citing Census); the band 'aging' is a judgement (no national median was re-checked here).
migration_notes: Growth of about 11% in five years at a median age above 44 implies in-migration; Louisa's growth is attributed to retirees settling near Lake Anna and to commuting access to Richmond, Fredericksburg and Charlottesville (Wikipedia). Not measured from migration flows.
rural_density_notes: 34.8 per km2 of land (Census 2020, 3 counties); Louisa 29.3, Fluvanna 36.6, Orange 41.0; GHSL 2030 33.1. Borderline low/moderate by the slate's own bands.
source: US Census 2020 (TIGERweb), Weldon Cooper Center projections July 2025, Wikipedia county articles for 2025 estimates and median age
gaps: 2025 estimates and median ages taken from Wikipedia citing the Census (Census API needs a key); migration flows not measured.

population_trend_notes: Statistics Canada July 1 estimates for the eight census divisions: 203,798 (2001), 197,170 (2019), 199,319 (2021), 204,755 (2025): -3.3% over 2001-2019, then +3.8% over 2019-2025; every MRC grew 2021-2025 (+0.9% La Matapédia to +4.9% Rimouski-Neigette). The long-run level is still near 2001.
median_age_notes: 2021 Census median age by MRC 46.8 (Rivière-du-Loup) to 56.8 (Les Basques), Québec 43.2; 65 and over 27.6% (23.7% in 2016; Québec 20.6%).
migration_notes: 2023/2024, eight census divisions: births 1,413, deaths 2,445 (natural decrease 1,032); net intraprovincial +747, net interprovincial +44, immigrants 285, net non-permanent residents +1,794. Intraprovincial inflow peaked at +1,602 in 2020/2021; it was slightly negative in 2015/2016 to 2017/2018 (-2, -169, -132).
rural_density_notes: 9.0 p/km² by the 2021 census (199,039 on 22,188 km²), about 6.0 outside the cities of Rimouski and Rivière-du-Loup; MRC densities 3.3 (La Matapédia) to 27.7 (Rivière-du-Loup).
gaps: 2026 Census not yet released; 2023/2024 components are the latest published; migration by age not analysed.

population_trend_notes: Seven-county total 81,485 (Census 2010) to 77,567 (Census 2020), -4.8 percent; ACS 2020-2024 5-year estimates sum to 76,874. Six of seven counties fell 2010-2020 (Schuyler -9.0, Clark -7.1, Lee -6.4, Van Buren -4.8, Appanoose -4.4, Scotland -2.6); Davis County rose 4.1 percent.
median_age_notes: ACS 2020-2024 5-year median age: Van Buren 44.7, Lee 43.6, Appanoose 43.5, Clark 43.5, Schuyler 39.2, Scotland 36.5, Davis 36.3; ACS 2024 1-year comparators: United States 39.2, Iowa 39.0, Missouri 39.4.
migration_notes: No migration series was opened.
rural_density_notes: Census 2020: 9.2 persons/km2 over the seven counties (land area 8,418 km2); 6.2 without Lee County (Keokuk, Fort Madison); county range 4.2 (Scotland) to 25.0 (Lee). GHSL 2030 projection 9.7.
source: US Census Bureau 2010 and 2020 decennial counts (TIGERweb); ACS 2020-2024 5-year via Census Reporter
gaps: Migration flows, cause of decline, and farm-consolidation data not retrieved; the pre-research description of 'shrinking small towns' is supported by the county counts but town-level figures were not opened.

population_trend_notes: Census 32,856 (2010) to 31,095 (2020), -5.4%; estimates since: 31,107 base (April 2020), 31,507 (2022), 31,383 (2024). Deaths exceed births every year (2024: 260 births, 604 deaths, natural change -344), offset by net migration (2024 +286: domestic +231, international +55; 2022 +590). From 2012 to 2018 migration was net out (-43 to -140 a year, Vintage 2020 series).
median_age_notes: Median age 48.6 and 27.2% aged 65 or over on 1 July 2024 (8,537 of 31,383), against 23.5% for Maine as a whole (330,265 of 1,405,012, summed from the same county file); median age was 48.5 in 2020, so the level is high but not rising fast.
migration_notes: Net in since 2019: +250 in 2019 and +335 in 2020 (Vintage 2020 series), +347 in 2021, +590 in 2022, +291 in 2023 and +286 in 2024 (Vintage 2024 series); net out 2012-2018. Domestic migration counts moves from any other US county, including other Maine counties; it is not a count of out-of-state buyers. Newcomers meet a county where an estimated 59% of households cannot afford to buy.
rural_density_notes: 4.7 persons/km2 on land area (2020 Census); GHSL 2030 5.4; largest centres small (Calais, Machias, Eastport).
source: US Census Bureau Population Estimates Vintage 2024 (co-est2024-alldata, cc-est2024-agesex-all) and Vintage 2020 (co-est2020-alldata); 2020 Census via TIGERweb
gaps: Migration is estimates-based and domestic includes in-state moves; income and housing tenure not pulled (ACS needs an API key).
